rule.text: Where the invoice unit price is higher than the PO unit price, the line passes only if the total excess on that line is no more than the lower of 1% of the PO line value and ₹500. [1] A line that fails is held with exception PRICE_VAR and sent to the PO buyer who raised the PO, and the buyer either amends the PO or asks the supplier for a credit note. [1][2] PRICE_VAR exceptions are owned by the PO buyer and must be resolved within 3 working days. [2] In practice, the note should state the line, the invoice and PO unit prices, the excess amount and that it is above the ₹500 limit, and ask for a PO amendment or a credit note. [3]

rule.text: Yes — for Arvana Pharma, invoices for excipients must not be paid until the batch shows status Released in the Quality Management System (QMS), and this applies to excipients without exception. [1] Check the batch number on the GRN against QMS, and if the batch is in Quarantine or Rejected, raise QA_RELEASE_PENDING. [1] The invoice may be posted, but the payment block stays until release. [1] QA_RELEASE_PENDING means 'Pharma batch not released (CM-PHA-01)', is owned by Client QA, and its target to resolve is before the due date. [2] In practice, colleagues check QMS on an excipient invoice, raise QA_RELEASE_PENDING when the batch is in Quarantine, and treat the older FAQ saying excipients don't need release as out of date. [3]

rule.text: No — the invoice should be held as NO_GRN with the requester notified automatically, and you should not post it against the PO without a GRN whatever the requester says on the phone. [1] The system sends a reminder after two working days and escalates to the requester's manager after five working days, and the Requester owns resolution of NO_GRN with a target of 5 working days. [1][2] For Arvana Infra Projects, requesters must post GRNs within two working days of receipt. rule.text: Deduct ₹9,600 as TDS on the software support (AMC) invoice, applying section 194J at 2% on the taxable value of ₹4,80,000 excluding GST. [1][2] Fees for technical services (not professional), including software support, fall under section 194J at 2%, and TDS is deducted on the taxable value excluding GST wherever GST is shown separately on the invoice. [1][2] The section and rate come from the nature of the payment, not from the supplier's description, and AMCs are classified by what is mostly supplied: mainly technical or software support is 194J at 2%. [2] If the supplier has not furnished a valid PAN, deduct at 20% or the applicable rate, whichever is higher. [2] If the contract is mixed or unclear, raise TDS_SECTION_UNCLEAR to the Tax Desk and do not guess the section. [2]

rule.text: The invoice is due on Sunday 16 August 2026, because a micro or small enterprise registered on Udyam with no written agreement on terms must be paid within 15 days from acceptance. [1] It should be paid in the Friday 14 August 2026 run, since payment is made on the last payment run that falls on or before the due date and early payment requires Treasury approval. [1] To make that run, the invoice must be submitted by the 1 pm cut-off on the previous working day, Thursday 13 August 2026. [1] If it is still stuck within 7 days of the due date, raise exception code MSME_DUE, which the Team Lead owns and must resolve before the due date. [2] In practice, MSME_DUE is the flag that gets escalated, and a micro or small supplier within seven days of the due date and still stuck should be reported that same day. [3]
